t: Depth Estimation Engine - public implementations survey
title: Depth Estimation Engine - public implementations survey
definition: Estimates scene depth from supported visual inputs.
description:
Depth Estimation Engine is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Estimates scene depth from supported visual inputs. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Depth Estimation Engine. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Depth Estimation Engine. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Depth Estimation Engine capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Depth Estimation
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Depth Estimation
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Depth Estimation Engine from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Depth Estimation Engine from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the Depth Estimation Engine needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.
